question.problem: The solution to the inequality $2<9y-7$ is $y${{field-1}}{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
First, we apply the addition principle, adding $7$ to both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & <9y-7 \\ 2+7 & <9y-7+7 \\ 9 & <9y+0 \\ 9 & <9y\end{aligned}
$$

Second, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $9:$

$$
\begin{aligned}9 & <9y \\ \frac{9}{9} & <\frac{9y}{9} \\ 1 & <\frac{\cancel{9}y}{\cancel{9}} \\ 1 & <y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, let's swap the left and right-hand sides so that the variable is on the left-hand side. Remember, we also need to flip the inequality.

$$
y>1
$$

Therefore, the solution is $y>1.$
